claims.text: Oxidation resistance and sustained material integrity in high-temperature multiprincipal-element alloys are primarily governed by the ability to form a slow-growing, adherent, self-healing oxide layer.
Cr and Al promote the formation of protective Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scales.
Protective Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scales slow oxygen diffusion.
Protective oxide scales reduce internal oxidation.
Increasing Cr and/or Al while holding microstructural features similar will alter protective-scale formation and evolution.
A coherent, adherent scale composed predominantly of Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3 acts as a physical and chemical barrier to oxygen ingress.
Higher Cr and/or Al levels enable the formation of more protective oxide films.
The resulting protective films reduce cation and oxygen diffusion rates.
The resulting protective films can self-heal after minor scale damage.
Reduced diffusion and scale self-healing lower the oxidation rate and preserve the integrity of the underlying alloy.
Cr/Al-enriched alloys will form more adherent protective scales than lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Cr/Al-enriched alloys will form thicker protective scales than lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Protective-scale growth will be slower in Cr/Al-enriched alloys than in lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Cr/Al-enriched alloys will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Cr/Al-enriched alloys will retain their mechanical properties better over time than lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys will form less protective scales or undergo faster scale growth.
The proposed governing behavior is expected to apply when high-temperature oxidation kinetics dominate.
The proposed behavior may not apply at low temperature, under non-oxidizing conditions, or when additional corrosive agents alter scale formation.
Direct correlations between alloying changes and protective-scale properties in multiprincipal-element alloys have limited corroborative evidence.
The individual roles of Cr and Al and their possible synergistic effects are uncertain.

contradictions.description: Under the same exposure duration, the enriched alloys are predicted to have both slower-growing and thicker scales, while the baseline is predicted to undergo faster scale growth. Without an additional explanation such as different initial scale formation or density, the thickness prediction conflicts with the stated growth-rate ordering.
